content.title: BitGo Stock Rises After IPO, Defying Recent Crypto Downturn
content.summary: Shares of BitGo traded 25% higher in the crypto-infrastructure firm’s New York Stock Exchange debut, marking the first major test for a digital-asset company IPO since the sector’s market downturn last year.

content.title: Trump pushes for lower rates and ban on investor home purchases in bid to make homes more affordable
content.summary: President Donald Trump 's plans for bringing homeownership within reach of more Americans involve pushing for lower interest rates on home loans and credit cards, and banning large institutional investors from buying single-family homes.  In his address Wednesday at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, Trump outlined four policies his administration is pursuing in a bid to make homeownership more affordable.  The U.S. housing market has been in a sales slump dating back to 2022, when mortgage rates began to climb from pandemic-era lows.

content.title: Trump doesn’t want America to be ‘a nation of renters,’ but experts say at least one of his proposals may put homeownership more out of reach
content.summary: Experts told Fortune Trump’s proposal allowing Americans to tap their 401(k) for down payments could inflate prices and leave Americans poorer in retirement.

content.title: Executive Order Takes a Step Toward Ban on Big Investors Buying Single-Family Homes
content.summary: The White House moved toward implementing President Donald Trump's ban on large institutional investors buying single-family homes in an executive order issued Tuesday night.  The first step is deciding what "large institutional investor" and "single-family home" actually mean.  The order, issued before Trump speaks about affordability at the World Economic Forum, charges the Treasury secretary and the assistant to the president for economic policy with developing definitions of "large institutional investor" and "single family home" within thirty days.

content.summary: AkademikerPension’s chief investment officer said the move was driven by the U.S. government’s poor finances, but that Trump’s action didn’t make the call more difficult.

content.title: Higher Treasury Yields Weigh on Home Builder Stocks
content.summary: A higher 10-year Treasury yield means higher mortgage rates.  The iShares U.S. Home Construction ETF was 1.5% lower in mid-morning trading, on pace for its largest percentage decline since Jan. 7, according to Dow Jones Market Data.  Builder stocks had been riding a wave of optimism spurred by a decline in mortgage rates earlier this month.

content.title: Trump Affordability Pitch Heads to Davos Fixed on Greenland
content.summary: Trump has vowed to unveil details of a sprawling affordability pitch — which has landed Wall Street banks, technology companies and home builders in his crosshairs — during a Wednesday speech at the World Economic Forum.  If he follows through on that pledge, it will come after a weekend in which he put Europe on edge over his increasingly aggressive rhetoric about winning control of Greenland — and his threat to use tariffs against a host of NATO allies backing the island’s ties to Denmark.  On Monday, with Europeans planning a separate meeting to respond to Trump and Danish officials skipping Davos, the president appeared to be trying to get affordability back on peoples’ minds with social media posts about mortgage rates and his economic agenda.

content.title: To Make Homes Affordable Again, Someone Has to Lose Out
content.summary: Trapped renters want home prices to fall so they can finally get onto the property ladder.  President  Trump  is heeding anger about housing affordability ahead of the midterm elections, and the administration has been drip-feeding ideas about how to tackle the issue.  Earlier this month, Trump suggested banning Wall Street investors from buying any more single-family homes.
